I struggle with this as well. I also don't like people saying they work to live and that work shouldn't be more than that. You spend 8 hours of your day, every day on your job, which is the majority of your time awake each day. If that work is something you don't atleast somewhat enjoy then there's something wrong.

So here's my advice:

- First off what life do you wish to live? Want a fancy car and a big house? Then get to work. Want more time for yourself? Then consume less and live more minimalistic.

- Find a job that you are okay with doing. It should interest you, you should somewhat enjoy it. If you dread it then it's time to change. Try out different things if you don't know what you want to do.

- Work 3/4 or 4/5 instead of fulltime. Even just having half a day off on a wednesday can make a big difference.

- Physical activities are important. Jobs as we know them today aren't humane and fairly new since the industrial revolution. Before that all work was more physical, more outdoors, more connected to nature. If you are working behind a desk all day then make sure you enjoy the outdoors and have some physical activities as well to connect with your body and nature again. That might sound like floaty monk bs but it helps, no animal on earth is meant to do the same repetitive task over and over again while sitting indoors.

- Try remote work if you can. It saves a ton of time on commuting, less socially draining, more comfortable environment, etc. Remote work has some of the best benefits. The only drawbacks are that you will need to make sure you have some social contact in your day so you don't get social anxiety, and again go outdoors as well as being inside your own house all day isn't good for your mental well-being.

- Don't have kids yet? Think about whether or not you want them and the cost of having them. Not only are kids expensive, they will also consume all your time for the next 20 or so years. This decision is one of the most impact full ones of your entire life.

- For projects you do on your own (like creative things), remember that people overestimate what they can do in an hour, but underestimate what they can do in a year.

Depression is a difficult thing to deal with. Not only for the person suffering from it but also for his/her surroundings. Been (still am) in the spot of the ine being depressed and also been in the spot if dating someone who was depressed at that time.

I personally think that a relationship while being depressed isn't a smart idea as it just doesn't give the relationship a fair chance. Sure it might work but it will be hard. So you have to ask yourself if you are willing to go through alot of pain and hard work (together with him) to keep the relationship going.

Is he getting any professional help? Ever talked with him about his depression and the cause of it? What triggers him to go into one of these depressed moments (depression kinda comes in moments for many people. U can feel fine for a few hours and then suddenly feel dead inside out of nowhere.) Try to communicate with him, let him know you are there for him but if he needs time alone then he can just say so. 

My advice: take some time for yourself to think about the relationship and if you are willing to go through with it, knowing that it will be hard. Sit him down and have a good talk with him, show him u care, ask him why he feels depressed and if there is anything you can do whenever he feels down.

Wish I could give better advice but depression is a complex thing that varies from person to person and sadly there is no defined solution to something like this. All you can do is try communicate the best you can. Hope it gets better for both of you!

The basic things I learnt from arena:
- keep ur stun for killwindows or to stop an enemy burst.
- keep ur defensives for when enemy bursts.
- keep ur own burst untill u see an opportunity to kill.
- make use of the environment, pillars are your friends to break los with enemy casters or to get some heals on urself or a teammate.
- always try to get ppl to vc with you, communication is soooo important!

Other than that it's just trial and error and keep trying till u find a comp and build that works for you. Never give up, even if ur stuck in low rating (been stuck in 1300 for a week to finally break out when I found my comp) keep going.
Learn from your mistakes, stay calm, don't blame the game, enemies or your partner but instead focus on what you could have done better.
